title: Adaptive input visibility & autofill resilience for compact and dense forms
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem statement: Browsers' autofill and password managers interact inconsistently with our current input affordances in compact and dense modes. We see clipped suggestion popovers, conflicting prefix/suffix overlays, and inconsistent label/placeholder collapse behavior that causes users to lose context when autofill triggers. This ticket scopes a set of design and token-level changes to make input visibility (prefix/suffix, reveal/clear controls) coexist with browser autofill suggestions across density variants, while preserving accessibility and motion/contrast tokens.
background_and_context: Design tokens for focus, z-index, and spacing have drifted between compact and default density. Recent QA surfaced issues: 1) password reveal icon overlaps browser autofill dropdown on Chrome with compact inputs, 2) helper text can be obscured when autofill inserts content before onChange events, 3) voiceover focus order jumps when browser suggestions are inserted. Engineering ENG-5521 has a runtime patch that delays certain DOM mutations; we must align visual spec + token changes and create migration guidance for integrators.
goals: Define token set and z-index ordering for prefix/suffix, autofill overlays, and browser suggestion stacks
Specify accessible affordance patterns for reveal/clear controls that do not break autofill behavior
Provide implementation guidance and CSS fallbacks for compact/dense variants
Ship design spec and migration checklist for product teams by release date
out_of_scope: Rewriting browser autofill behavior (impossible); deep changes to form frameworks used by individual product teams beyond suggested integration patterns.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: We will not hide browser autofill suggestions — instead we change input affordance layering and spacing so suggestions remain visible and contextual.
Prefer token adjustments (spacing, focus ring thickness, icon touch-target offsets) over adding heavy JS that intercepts autofill events to avoid regressions and performance costs.

For password reveal, adopt a larger hit target placed inside suffix container with explicit aria-label and ensure the suffix sits above input background but below browser suggestion z-order (documented with required z-index values).
Motion: avoid animated repositioning of helper text when autofill triggers to reduce layout shift; prefer fade-in for helper/helper-success state when necessary.
Accessibility: preserve DOM order so screen readers announce label -> input -> helper -> error in a stable sequence; use aria-live for non-critical live updates only.
engineering_notes_and_implementation_gui: Token changes: define token.input.compact.suffixOffset, token.input.compact.leadingPadding, token.input.zIndex.suffix = 600, token.input.zIndex.autofillOverlay = 700
CSS fallback: use ::-webkit-autofill styling guidance and explicit painting of background to avoid sudden color snaps; include comment with Chrome bug workarounds
Preferred pattern for reveal buttons: button element inside .input__suffix with aria-pressed for toggle state; do not inject reveal with absolute positioning that alters DOM order.
Edge cases: when prefix contains inline icons, compress prefix padding rather than float the icon over the suggestion box to avoid overlap.
acceptance_criteria: Compact and default density input tokens are documented in the design token table and consumed by CSS variables
Figma spec shows z-index and spacing overlays with annotated keyboard & touch targets
QA test plan covers Chrome/Firefox/Safari autofill, password managers (1Password, Bitwarden), and VoiceOver/JAWS screen reader flows
Two product pages (forms-checkout, account-settings) implemented the pattern with no visual overlap reported in staging
Design review sign-off by Samir Patel (PM) and Lina Park (Accessibility)
PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/1234 and integration PRs linked in product stories
